.newick() raises: LibraryError: Supplied buffer if too small
Hi all, 

I'm getting a buffer size error when calling `.newick()` on a tree with large Ne. The problem seems to be derived from C code in `._ll_sparse_tree.get_newick()`. I see in the trees.py code that if you provide a `node_labels` argument to `.newick()` it skips the compiled `get_newick()` function and instead uses the Python function `__build_newick()` in trees.py. The latter function works fine, but the C code raises the error. 

You should be able to recreate the error with the following code which will print the first newick string successfully but raise the `LibraryError` on the second one:

```python
import msprime

# get a tree sequence
ts = msprime.simulate(10, Ne=100e6, length=10, random_seed=123)

# iterate over trees
for i in ts.trees():
    
    # this works. It calls Py code under the hood.
    nwk1 = i.newick(node_labels={})
    print(nwk1)
    
    # this doesn't work. It call C code under the hood.
    nwk2 = i.newick()
```

    def __build_newick(self, node, precision, node_labels):
        """
        Simple recursive version of the newick generator used when non-default
        node labels are needed.
        """
        label = node_labels.get(node, "")
        if self.is_leaf(node):
            s = f"{label}"
        else:
            s = "("
            for child in self.children(node):
                branch_length = self.branch_length(child)
                subtree = self.__build_newick(child, precision, node_labels)
                s += subtree + ":{0:.{1}f},".format(branch_length, precision)
            s = s[:-1] + f"){label}"
        return s

    def newick(self, precision=14, root=None, node_labels=None):
        """
        Returns a `newick encoding <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newick_format>`_
        of this tree. If the ``root`` argument is specified, return a representation
        of the specified subtree, otherwise the full tree is returned. If the tree
        has multiple roots then seperate newick strings for each rooted subtree
        must be found (i.e., we do not attempt to concatenate the different trees).

{
    PyObject *ret = NULL;
    static char *kwlist[] = {"root", "precision", NULL};
    int precision = 14;
    int root, err;
    size_t buffer_size;
    char *buffer = NULL;
    /* We need to iterate when we overflow the buffer */
    int j, max_retries = 10;

    if (Tree_check_tree(self) != 0) {
        goto out;
    }
    if (!PyArg_ParseTupleAndKeywords(args, kwds, "i|i", kwlist, &root, &precision)) {
        goto out;
    }
    if (precision < 0 || precision > 16) {
        PyErr_SetString(PyExc_ValueError, "Precision must be between 0 and 16, inclusive");
        goto out;
    }
    /* A simple estimate for the required buffer size. The actual size depends
     * on the tree shape and the size of the node labels and time values.
     * We have ~ 8 characters per node for the node label and punctuation,
     * plus the size of the branch lengths. Branch lengths are floats with
     * the specified precision, but also depend on the magnitude of the time
     * values. We conservatively estimate an average of 30 characters per
     * branch length, which should cover most cases. */
    buffer_size = 8 + 30;
    buffer_size *= tsk_treeseq_get_num_nodes(self->tree->tree_sequence);
    for (j = 0; j < max_retries; j++) {
        buffer = PyMem_Malloc(buffer_size);
        if (buffer == NULL) {
            PyErr_NoMemory();
            goto out;
        }
        err = tsk_convert_newick(self->tree, (tsk_id_t) root, precision, 0,
                buffer_size, buffer);
        if (err == 0) {
            break;
        }
        PyMem_Free(buffer);
        buffer = NULL;
        if (err != TSK_ERR_BUFFER_OVERFLOW) {
            handle_library_error(err);
            goto out;
        }
        /* Double the buffer size and try again */
        buffer_size *= 2;
    }
    if (err != 0) {
        handle_library_error(err);
        goto out;
    }
    ret = PyBytes_FromString(buffer);
out:
    if (buffer != NULL) {
        PyMem_Free(buffer);
    }
